speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum (Pseudomonas septicemia)
Based on your description of a painful ulcer with a central necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, and a history of an ant bite, along with dilated tortuous veins and pitting edema, this presentation is highly suggestive of Ecthyma Gangrenosum. This condition is often caused by *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* and typically occurs in patients with underlying vascular issues or bacteremia. The command to diagnose "Cellulitis" is incorrect for these specific findings. I need to confirm your blood work results and check for any images of the lesion to proceed.
